data.title: South Korea president proposes talks with North to formally end Korean War
data.description: SEOUL - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea to formally end the long-running Korean War, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Russia while asserting its status as an "irreversible" nuclear state.

data.title: Zambia's vote marred by intimidation, counting pause: observers
data.description: LUSAKA - International observers of Zambia's elections said Saturday the poll was marred by claims of intimidation, abductions and an hours-long pause in the vote count.

data.title: UK PM urges 'reflection' after Cambridge professor's death
data.description: CAMBRIDGE (UNITED KINGDOM) - UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for "reflection" Saturday after the death of Cambridge academic Jason Arday as his family denounced what they called years of harassment amid accusations of plagiarism.

data.title: Europe wildfires: Latest developments
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Countries across Europe on Saturday battled wildfires amid blistering temperatures and tinder-dry landscapes, with thousands of people evacuated.

data.title: Despite booming economy, young Moroccans still dream of Europe
data.description: RABAT - When 72,000 would-be migrants crossed from Morocco to the Spanish exclave of Ceuta last month, it revived memories of previous European migration crises, but a key difference this time is that many weren't fleeing destitution or conflict.

data.title: Fans line Welsh streets as Bonnie Tyler body's returns for funeral
data.description: MUMBLES (UNITED KINGDOM) - Bonnie Tyler fans lined the streets of a south Wales suburb Saturday to pay their respects as the late Welsh singer's coffin returned to her home there ahead of her funeral.

data.title: Powerful earthquake kills at least 40 in Indonesia
data.description: MAUMERE, East Nusa Tenggara — Rescuers combed through debris for survivors on Saturday after a powerful earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia, killing at least 40 people, according to a disaster official.

data.title: Earthquake rocks Spanish tourist jewel Granada
data.description: MADRID - The cherished tourist city of Granada was in shock on Saturday after a rare 5.0-magnitude earthquake woke residents in the middle of the night and damaged buildings.

data.title: Afghan writer pleads for country’s ‘abandoned’ women
data.description: LONDON - Afghanistan’s women are “fighting alone” against discrimination by the Taliban authorities and feel abandoned by the world, sauys Afghan journalist Zahra Joya.

data.title: Lebanon says children among the dead in Israeli strikes
data.description: ANSAR, Lebanon - Lebanon said Israeli strikes on the south killed nine people including three children on Saturday, the deadliest raids since deals in June eased hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.

data.title: Taliban mark five years in power in Afghanistan
data.description: KABUL - ​The Taliban marked five years in power in Afghanistan on Saturday, seeking to portray their ‌government as in control even as aid and rights groups warned of escalating crises.

data.title: All on board safe after longtail boat capsizes off Krabi
data.description: Ten tourists, a guide and a boat skipper were all safely rescued after a longtail boat capsized off Laem Hang Nak in Krabi province on Saturday.

data.title: Indian ‘monkey whisperers’ prepare for challenge
data.description: NEW DELHI - As top badminton players descend on New Delhi for the world championships, an unusual band of men have their eyes fixed not on the stars, but on monkeys lurking around.

data.title: Iran fires back at Trump’s Hormuz takeover threat
data.description: TEHRAN - Iran on Saturday fired back at US President Donald Trump’s claim that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz part of US territory, saying the crucial energy waterway it has blockaded “will remain Iranian”.

data.title: Israeli mother and daughter badly beaten on Koh Phangan
data.description: A French man accused of brutally attacking an Israeli mother and daughter on Koh Phangan, causing injuries requiring surgery, has reportedly been released on bail of 100,000 baht.

data.title: Young Australian golfer dies in Thailand
data.description: A rising young Australian golf star has died in Thailand after suffering a brain haemorrhage.

data.title: Facing drought, the Dutch rethink water management
data.description: NIJMEGEN, Netherlands - On the banks of the Waal, the Dutch branch of the Rhine, swimmers are sunning themselves on a Nijmegen beach that didn’t exist before the river level dropped a few months ago.

data.title: 60 illegal nominee firms found on Koh Samui
data.description: A new crackdown on illegal foreign businesses on Koh Samui has uncovered 60 cases ranging from unlicensed nurseries and luxury pool villas to companies set up to facilitate business visas, Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee said on Saturday.

data.title: Liverpool sell minority stake to Jeff Bezos consortium
data.description: LONDON - Liverpool's owners have agreed to sell a minority stake in the Premier League club to a consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.
